thread:
Maya: :rotating_light: Heads up — dedicated pool `dedicated-us-west2-prod` hit 100% GPU utilization ~2m ago and requests started spilling to hosted. p95 token latency jumped 120ms -> ~420ms. Customers reporting throttles. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/infra/pools/dedicated-us-west2-prod

Jamal: I'm on it, looking at autoscaler and node events. pinging cloud infra team.

Sofia: Any signs of preemptible churn or long pending pods?

Maya: Node count steady, pods are pending due to GPU allocation failures (Insufficient GPUs). No OOMs.

Tom: I see an uptick in network errors between control-plane and kubelets in us-west-2 from cloud provider metrics — looks like an AZ-level networking flakiness. That would explain nodes reporting capacity but not accepting pods.

Deploy Bot: Incident created #INC-3421 (automated) — dedicated-pool-exhaustion-us-west2.

Maya: @Jamal can we temporarily prefer another dedicated pool (us-east-1) before we force more hosted spillover? Hosted costs spike and some customers are sensitive to model variant fallbacks.

Jamal: We can shift routing weights. Trying to patch route table now. Doing a dry-run first.

Sofia: If control-plane connectivity is flaky, shifting traffic might not help for stateful KV caches pinned to the us-west GPUs. We should check cache eviction policy.

Tom: Agreed. Suggest two steps in parallel: (1) shift new requests away from us-west2 dedicated to us-east1 dedicated, (2) reduce spillover threshold so hosted only used as last resort.

Rachel: Quick cost note — hosted spillover at current rate will increase monthly bill for this tenant class ~3x. Need to notify finance + account execs for impacted customers.

Oncall: Patch applied to routing: changed weight for pool `dedicated-us-east1-prod` +30% and reduced `spillover_threshold` on `dedicated-us-west2-prod` from 0.95 -> 0.99 to slow automatic spillover. Commands used: 
```bash
# shift weight towards us-east1
rwctl routing update --pool dedicated-us-east1-prod --delta-weight +30
# tighten spillover threshold
rwctl routing update --pool dedicated-us-west2-prod --spillover-threshold 0.99
```

Maya: After the change, p95 dropped to ~180ms for the affected routes. Hosted requests are decreasing. Still seeing some stuck KV-backed sessions.

Jamal: I'm launching a manual eviction/reshuffle job for pods in `dedicated-us-west2-prod` to free up fragmented GPUs. Running now: 
```bash
kubectl label node <node> maintenance=true && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Sofia: Also bumping cache eviction TTL for prefix caches to 30s to prevent hot KV saturation while we reshuffle.

Tom: Cloud provider confirms an ongoing networking degradation in one AZ, still investigating. They recommended moving traffic off the AZ; we've already shifted to other AZs in the region where possible.

Rachel: Notifying top 5 customers on the affected list + AMs. Draft sent for review.

Incident Bot: @channel INC-3421 assigned to Jamal (oncall). Priority: P1 - degraded capacity + customer impact.

Jamal: Manual reshuffle finished — freed 4 GPUs, some pods successfully rescheduled. p95 stabilizing around 150-200ms. We're keeping spillover tightened for now.

Maya: Can we schedule a capacity top-up for dedicated-us-west2-prod? If this recurs during peak hours we need permanent scale.

Oncall: Opening infra task to provision +2 GPU nodes to dedicated-us-west2-prod and to run a postmortem. Ticket: INFRA-892. ETA for capacity add ~45m (spin up + validation).

Tom: Follow-ups: (1) validate routing failover docs (we had a few manual steps), (2) add automated preference for regional dedicated fallback before hosted spillover, (3) cost alerting when hosted spillover > X tokens/hr.

Maya: Thanks all. I'll keep monitoring and update INC-3421. If anything spikes again, re-open with @oncall. :thumbsup:
